name: Iron Age
description: Upgrade the Bronze industrial workshop using Wrought Iron.

pages.text: $(bold)Entering Iron Age$()$(br2)The Bronze workshop produces your first Wrought Iron Ingot: concentrate Magnetite, reduce it with charcoal, Calcite flux, HEAT and AIR in the Bloomery, reheat the Iron Bloom in the Refractory Kiln, then consolidate it in the powered Forge Hammer before the hot timer expires.$(br2)Unlike vanilla smelting, this industrial chain is your Iron Age starting point.

$(bold)Your first Iron machine upgrade$()$(br2)Use Wrought Iron Ingots to make a longer-lived forging die for your EXISTING Bronze Forge Hammer.$(br2)The Bronze die provides 384 successful batches; the Wrought Iron die lasts 768. It does not increase RPM, torque, processing output or the machine's mechanical power.

pages.title: Wrought Iron Forging Die
pages.text: Four Wrought Iron Ingots and a polished blackstone anvil insert. Right-click a formed Bronze Forge Hammer with the die to install it. This consumes the replacement die, even when replacing an existing bronze part.

$(bold)Servicing the Hammer$()$(br2)Sneak-right-click the formed Forge Hammer with an empty hand to inspect installed die material and remaining batches. Right-click normally while holding a replacement Bronze or Wrought Iron die to service the machine.$(br2)Wear advances only after a completed workpiece; stalled or idle power does not consume die life. Existing Bronze dies and saved machine wear remain usable.

$(bold)Iron 0B — Heating Wrought Iron$()$(br2)A Wrought Iron Ingot leaves the Bronze-to-Iron consolidation chain cold. Feed ONE ingot into the EXISTING fueled Refractory Kiln. After 240 HEAT-supplied firing ticks, the same ingot gains a new 120-second forging-heat timer, visible on its tooltip. The kiln consumes actual fuel; the ingot does not become a second special item.

$(bold)Forging a Wrought Iron Plate$()$(br2)Move the still-hot ingot into the EXISTING powered Forge Hammer with a usable Bronze or Wrought Iron Forging Die. Gear V2 must supply at least 20 RPM and 6 torque for 160 supplied ticks. ONE hot ingot becomes ONE Wrought Iron Plate. Material quality is retained, but the temporary heat tag is removed. Cold or expired ingots must be reheated.

pages.title: First Wrought Iron Plate
pages.text: Produced through Kiln and Forge Hammer machine processing, visible in JEI. This is a full ingot-equivalent plate, not an ordinary crafting-table shortcut. Bars and rods are produced next in the existing Rolling Mill; structural Iron blocks follow.

$(bold)Toward stronger industry$()$(br2)The first Iron upgrade is longer-lived tooling. Stronger shafts, precision gears and heavier manufacturing are planned next, but require meaningful source and network load tests. A stronger part must not create power or bypass the limits of an existing wooden gear.

$(bold)Iron 0C — Rolling Wrought Iron$()$(br2)A hot Wrought Iron Ingot can enter the existing powered Bronze Rolling Mill instead of the Forge Hammer. At 16 RPM and 6 torque, 180 supplied ticks produce ONE Wrought Iron Bar. This is a shaped billet rolling process; the Forge Hammer still makes Plates from the same heated ingot.

$(bold)Smaller Iron Rods$()$(br2)Bars must be heated again in the fueled Refractory Kiln for 240 HEAT-supplied ticks. Feed a HOT Bar to the Rolling Mill: 200 supplied ticks at 16 RPM and 6 torque produce FOUR slender Wrought Iron Rods. One bar represents one ingot-equivalent; each rod represents one quarter. Heat expires in world time, and the output retains material quality but does not stay hot. The original Copper Sheet recipe works cold.

pages.title: Forged and Rolled Bar
pages.text: Roll one hot Wrought Iron Ingot in the existing Bronze Rolling Mill. Use the Bar for structural metal and precise wrought rod production. Recipes are machine processing entries in JEI.

pages.title: Iron Rod Stock
pages.text: Four slim rods from one heated Bar. Iron Rods will become fasteners and supports for the first Iron factory building pieces.
